rationale: Lyc qualitative of ⲱⲛⲧ̄/ϫⲱⲛⲧ 'knead' (Crum 776). In Manichaean cosmological-anthropological register, the soul is 'kneaded into' the flesh of Sin — the dough metaphor for the entanglement of light-substance in matter. Distinct from ⲗⲱⲃϣ 'mingle' (cosmic-elemental register) and ⲙⲟⲩⲝⲧ̄ 'be mingled' (already in glossary).

From ⲉⲧⲡⲱ 'weight, load' (Crum). Used twice on this page in the construction 'they bear under a great burden upon their shoulders' (lines 17-18, 20-21). The holy ones bearing the burden of flesh — central image of this paraenetic kephalaion.

Compound: ⲛⲁⲟ́ⲥ (Lyc qualitative of ⲛⲟϭ 'be great') + ⲛ̄ϩⲏⲧ 'of heart' = 'great-of-heart' in pejorative sense = haughty, proud. Fits the moral catalogue of bad-heart states (paired with ⲃⲁⲗⲕ 'wroth').
Abstract ⲙⲛⲧ- + ϩⲗⲟϭ-ϩⲏⲧ 'sweet-heart' = sweetness-of-heart, gentleness. Lyc ⲟ́ for ϭ. The affective-virtuous pair-partner with ἀγάπη in the holy ones' response to the sinner.
Lyc reflex of ϩⲁⲧ 'silver' (already in accumulated vocab as ⲉϩⲁⲧ in different register). Standard pair with ⲡⲛⲟⲩⲃ 'gold' in the moral catalogue of worldly desires.

ⲣ̄- + Greek χολή 'gall, bile' as verb = 'be angry, become choleric' (humoral-medical register for anger). Listed alongside ⲱⲧⲁⲣⲧⲣ̄ 'be disturbed' and ⲃⲱⲗⲕ 'be wroth' as the cascade of negative affects.

Verb of unclear etymology in line 25. Soteriological context (hands loosed against the Cross of Light) demands a violence/harm verb. Possibly Lyc reflex of ⲱϣϭ 'stretch out (in violence)' or related harm-verb. Confidence low.

Reduplicated form of ⲛⲉϫ 'cast, throw' = iterative 'cast at' = deride/reproach. Used in negative-action catalogue: the holy ones do not deride the sinner. Standard Coptic reduplication-pattern for derisive action.
Idiom: ⲱⲡ 'count, reckon' + ϩⲣⲉⲕ (= ϩⲣⲱⲕ 'silence, stillness'). Crum lists ⲱⲡ ϩⲣⲱⲕ as 'be silent.' The patient response of the holy ones who decline to judge the sinner.
From ⲟⲩⲉ 'be far' with directional ⲁⲣⲁ⸗ = 'distance oneself from.' Standard Coptic spatial-relational verb. Listed in line 28-29 among the things the holy ones do NOT do to the sinner.
Lyc reflex of ϭⲓϫ 'hand' (with ⲝ for ϫ). Plural ⲛⲉⲕⲟ́ⲓⲝ 'your hands' in line 25. Distinct from accumulated ⲛⲟⲩⲭ/ⲡⲟⲩⲭⲓⲛ; here a different orthographic variant of ϭⲓϫ.
